correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the Legendre recurrence (RESULT.md:46–81). Integrating the derivative of the difference P_(n-1)-P_(n+1) against the exponential gives the first identity; integrating the spherical Legendre ODE and then the derivative of sin(theta)P_n gives the second, with zero endpoint terms. Eliminating the unweighted moments gives the two-step positive baseline. Multiplication by 2 cos²(theta)-1 and substitution give the stated R_n, with the low-degree zero terms omitted. The profile in z=n(n+1) is strictly increasing to its sole positive critical point and decreases to 1, giving the unique minimum at zero and the two candidate maximum degrees. The adjacent subtraction has the stated sign: its polynomial increases from a negative constant term to infinity, and a tie forces the continuous maximum strictly between the corresponding degrees. These disjoint intervals in z and the strictly increasing critical point give the strict switch ordering, no skips and no third tie. For large y, writing z=yc gives a limiting order-1/y profile 6(3c-2)/(c+1)², stationary at c=7/3; the O(y^-1/2) rounding error in c therefore contributes only O(y^-2) to R. Degree two gives the small-y asymptotic. Boundary coefficients are missing at finitely many degrees only: a zero-energy finite atomic measure would have the moments of a finite harmonic polynomial density and must vanish. Universality holds exactly with no missing degrees. The frozen numerical checker was inspected, not executed or treated as proof.
